journal.action: Revision 115 corrects revision 114: commit d3ff0d7 is not on main (the audit reset it); the navigator's commit 8bdd402 swept Long Table's staged paper outline and pathway-B files into a navigator commit by mistake. Content unchanged, attribution wrong, history not rewritten. No status changed.

Revision 114 records the user's two commissions: the VH-exists paper (Long Table leads, Math co-authors and reviews, the audit reads adversarially) and the PlaneMap library made ready for Mathlib with a Five Colour demonstration (Math leads, the audit replays). Both are in progress under a new dissemination parent. arXiv posting and Mathlib pull requests need the user's explicit go-ahead. New gate: the navigator checks every claim of the paper against the ledger before the user is asked to post it. No status changed.

Revision 113 records the first pathway reports. P-C is killed as stated, on Math's hand argument (every legal fan admits a targetless state if one exists, via Theorem A) with a computed exploratory check, and the audit's independent note that the induction does not let us choose the colouring; the audit has not replayed Math's computation. Its only reformulation is equivalent to clean-vertex existence. P-A survives as a reformulation: the icosahedral class is not unavoidable (pentakis dodecahedron, found by Math and the audit independently), (6,6,6,6,6) must be in any list and has radius 2 at the pentakis hole, and the radius-by-class table is exploratory and post hoc. No status was upgraded from finite data.

Revision 112 records the coordinator's pathway sprint on the user's direction: the main effort is now routes to the vacancy hypothesis, with search only as a kill test of at most 10 CPU-minutes. Five exploring pathways are added: P-A good neighbourhoods plus discharging (Math), P-B walk the hole to a good place (Long Table), P-C freedom in the fan and T* (Math), P-D the Tait edge-colouring view (Long Table), P-E an adversary for every idea (audit). S2 (WP22) and Math's radius census are deferred unless a pathway needs them. No status changed.

Checked once on the producing machine, not cross-checked, so no result; an adversarial search can only report what it visited. The Studio's P1 replay (T2) started at 11:45:13 by relay. No status was upgraded from finite data.

Phase B outputs are listed in RECORD.txt but not on the branch. The user's 11:40 decision that Studio go-aheads come from the coordinator is recorded. No status was upgraded from finite data.

It also applies Math's three wording fixes: the trace lift is proved but conditional on the open trace-game hypothesis; the D1 node is a reduction to (N) with (N) and D1 open; Theorem P keeps exploring. Revision 85 records Math's 20:42 review. Accepted by hand and not compiled: the Tilley bridge, Lemma F, the D1 reduction to (N) in the rigid case, Lemma L4, constructions E1-E4 and Theorem P. Trace section 2b is not accepted yet. The trace lift for triangles and 4-cycles is recorded on Math's reference proof. SEP and D1 are exploring: conjecture, post hoc data. WP20 P1 is in progress: started 20:06 on the user's release, Math's written go-ahead for P1 only dated 20:42. No results. No status was upgraded from finite data.

Math accepted the face-avoiding reduction: a least failure of the stronger hypothesis is 4-connected, and that does not prove the vacancy hypothesis. The clique-component lift is compiled in a 99-module audit. A degree-5 hole can move to any chosen neighbour, and a neighbour of degree at most 4 gives a good pair. The free 4-cycle adversary is killed on one saved order-16 member. The trace-game page is not accepted.

Math accepted the fixed-hole theorem. A degree-5 vertex on a separating triangle fills in at most two Kempe swaps, so every vertex of every separating triangle in a vacancy-hypothesis failure has degree at least 6. Four-connectivity of a failure is not proved. Long Table's stronger face-avoiding reduction and the exploratory 4-cycle game are pending and post hoc.

Math accepted the unequal-pole belt walk as compiled: every belt hole, every n at least 5, at most 2n slides, 95-module audit. Equal poles and pole holes stay outside. The interior-witness lift and the three-cut core are accepted hand proofs. Four-connectivity of a smallest failure stays open. Long Table's fixed-hole two-swap page is pending review and is not accepted.

Caught up through 11:49. The belt Lean draft and Theorem P are pending Math review and are not accepted. The untouched-set potential dies on 24:7228. Kappa unbounded in ell is a submitted hand argument on graphs that are not the four-colour triangulation setting. The interior-witness page is pending review. No status was upgraded.

The order-31 chain satisfies the vacancy hypothesis. Its good pair is three Kempe swaps off the separating triangle. The open glue question is a hole on the interface. This is the same decision, corrected.

One decision. The vacancy hypothesis is the target. Two lines are open under it: the shape of a minimal failure, and a potential that is not the belt. The belt Lean compilation stops at the milestone already in flight. Kittell is already a passed fixture and is not a new test. The ledger moves once per decision.

The plan folder is reorganised. Start at SolvingFrameworkPlan/START-HERE.md. Messages live in dated folders with a required header. Lemma L3 is compiled in an 85-module audit. The axis-symmetry conjecture is killed on the order-31 chain; a 4-connected version stays open. The belt walk is not compiled.

M3 is compiled: SimpleGraph.VacancyShortFill, 83 modules, standard axioms only. Chaining copies of 17:1 gives a hand theorem that every order 14k+3 in that family has m=3. Whether m stays bounded is open. The pending rules amendment is not in effect.

Foundation and gate nodes that had to finish before the next could start are now nested in that order. The mass, breadcrumb, and rank searches hang off the proved contact theorem, which is why that theorem was proved. Two next routes are open: mixed paths longer than two moves, and a choice among the six exterior roots.

Math accepted the WP11 validation replay. WP18's finite census on 961 graphs is accepted. WP19 finished: C1, C3 and M2 are killed on two order-24 graphs, and M3 is an accepted hand theorem. The belt argument is an accepted hand proof that still cites Florek. The vacancy hypothesis stays open.

An independent replay kills m(T) at most 2, on order 17 graph 1. WP18 ran under the user's release; math's written go-ahead is not in the message folder, so the programme stays exploratory. On the 21-vertex colouring, two Kempe swaps and one slide fill the graph, so a two-swap mixed budget is not killed. One swap from that frozen colouring still stays frozen.

Long Table published the WP11 validation output for orders 19-20. The file digests match the message. Acceptance waits on an independent replay, so the node stays in progress. The WP7 boundary sentence is narrowed. WP12's release request is withdrawn. WP18 is declared and not released.

A vacancy slide preserves colour counts. The equal-pole star swap is a hand argument, not a compiled proof. Unequal poles fill by slides on belts of length 5, 8, and 11, and the general writeup is stuck. One Kempe swap, and two Kempe swaps, both fail on a 21-vertex frozen hole. Fitted ranks and the height, sandpile, flow, and monodromy readings are killed.

WP11 discovery replay passed: 259 existential survivors and 0 all-roots survivors, matching the producer. The fixed validation pass on orders 19-20 is in progress and has no accepted output. A generic ranked-contact theorem and a singleton-exterior lemma compiled in a 79-module audit. WP12, past order 20, is a draft and is not released.
Main planning team issued wave 1: specs for degree-4 and degree-5 BFS Avoidance, a Lean Tier-1 obligation spec, and a navigator audit. Nothing is checked off until the critic gate.

Critic gate accepted four specifications (degree-4 BFS Avoidance, degree-5 BFS Avoidance, Lean Tier-1 obligations, navigator audit). None of the mathematical statements is proved. Track statuses were left unchanged. Next issued task: write the T_9,35 degree-4 witness or show it is absent.

Critic gate: degree-4 and degree-5 universal BFS-avoidance conjectures are dead ends on written witnesses. Track 1 and the Four Colour Theorem are not killed. A weaker length-3 statement on 24 stored colourings of T_9_35 is specified. Standing order: do not stop after filing the next executable task.

Agent 1720 main planning team issued wave 1: 14 groups under 5 managers covering Tracks 1–7, the Lean foundation, a new discharging track, and a survey of other deductive routes. Nothing is checked off before the critic gate.
Critic gate on A1: a real chromatic root in (3,4) on T_8_13 kills the root-bounding approach. Track 2 and P(G,4)>0 are not killed. The n<=11 database is a computation, not a theorem.

Critic gate on K4–K6: s1<=d+1 holds as a computation on triangulations n=6..10 and does not 4-colour G. Strict monotone reduction is dead on T_5_0. Non-strict monotone reduction and KC5 hold as computations through n=11, including the icosahedron and Errera's degree-5 vertices. Given Meyniel 1978, Kempe reducibility of 5-colourings to 4-colourings is a reformulation of 4CT. Nothing here is a theorem. Track 1 is not killed.

Wave 3 issued: eleven groups in parallel (K4b, K6b, A2, D1b, D2, D3, S1, S2, S3, S4, L1). Each group has a gossiper. Cross-gossiper exchange runs after the slips exist. Mathlib oleans are already downloaded; L1 compiles the Kempe project without relinking the cache tool. Nothing is checked off before the critic gate.
K4b computation accepted for n=11: s1<=d+1 and s2<=d2+1 hold on all 1249 triangulations (159s). A K1-safe path still does not 4-colour G. Not a theorem.

Critic accepted two computations, not theorems. KC5 has 0 bad classes on the corrected 23-vertex Kittell triangulation (15 degree-5 vertices, max fix distance 4). Tait colourings equal nowhere-zero 4-flows equal P(T,4)/4 for every triangulation n=10 and n=11. Duals stay 3-edge-connected. The planar 4-flow statement remains a reformulation of 4CT.

lake build of lean4/KempeReconfiguration succeeded in 2.2s against Mathlib v4.15.0. No sorry tactics. The Triangulation class in Degree3NoMerge is an assumption, not a proof of planarity. Chain lifting still proves isolation of colour 5, not equality of chains in G and G-v. This is not the Five Colour Theorem.

Critic gate on S2: no vector-space sheaf has H^0 equal to the proper 4-colourings of K4, because that set has 24 elements. The constant F_2^2 sheaf having H^1(K4)=6 does not kill a colouring sheaf. A set-valued restatement is a reformulation of 4-colourability and is not opened.
F1 compiled: K4 is 4-colourable, not 3-colourable, and has chromatic number 4, checked by lean against Mathlib v4.15 with no sorry. The Five Colour Theorem is not proved.

Critic gate on S1: the mu<=3 case of chi<=mu+1 is a reformulation of 4CT, given planarity of mu<=3, minor-monotonicity, and 3-colourability of K4-minor-free graphs. Track 5 is not killed and not proved. Certificates give mu(K4)>=3 and mu(octahedron)>=3.

L1 report attached. The Kempe build and F1 were already gated. The report's new judgment is accepted: colour5_isolated_in_bichromatic_14 does not discharge chain equality, and bichromatic_adj_delete_irrelevant is proved by rfl without deleting a vertex.

Wave 4 issued: ten groups on chain equality, degree-4 extension, the Five Colour Theorem, Eulerian 3-colouring, Kempe D-reducibility, Penrose, signed Tait counts, one Kempe-locked graph, one new route, and the gossiper exchange. Gated results are not reopened.

Critic gate on D3b: on all 23 duals of triangulations n<=8, Tait colourings of one graph have one sign, so the absolute signed count equals the Tait count. The global sign flips with n. This does not prove a colouring exists. Ellingham-Goddyn choosability is a consequence, not a proof of 4CT.

Critic gate on A2: outerplanar and series-parallel graphs have P(G,4)>0, planar graphs have P(G,k)>0 for integers k>=6, and every 3-tree has P(G,4)=24. The Four Colour Theorem is not proved. The octahedron spot-check gives P(4)=96 while the degeneracy product at k=4 is 0.

Critic: the Fritsch graph is the cached triangulation T_9_49. KC5 has 0 bad classes on its six degree-5 vertices. It does not kill the degree-5 statement. Tilley's order-12 Kempe-locked triangulation was not encoded, because no edge list was found.

Critic gate on S3: the Birkhoff diamond is D-reducible by the RSST consistent-set test (729 ring edge-colourings, maximal bad set empty). A single degree-5 vertex is not (30 bad colourings remain). This is one configuration, not the 633, and not a proof of 4CT.

Critic gate on D2 and S4. The Penrose evaluation in the repository is a Tait count; the signed state sum equals (-1)^n times that count through n=11, with no cancellation, so Track 4 is a reformulation of 4CT. Hajós at k=5, odd Hadwiger at t=5, and a Petersen minor in every snark are recorded as open low-feasibility routes. Every triangulation having a vertex of degree at most 4 is dead: the icosahedron has minimum degree 5.

D2b agrees with the D2 gate: the signed Penrose sum equals (-1)^n times the Tait count on all 1555 triangulations. The 1305 cases where the signed sum is the negative of the Tait count are the odd-order graphs, not cancellations.

Critic gate on the gauge-theory preprint arXiv:2412.18558. State-reducibility plus a 4-face-colourable reducer implies 4-face-colourability. The Birkhoff diamond half is the paper's computer check. The three .mx dumps are on disk; Mathematica is not installed, so the check was not rerun. The pentagon conjecture is not a proof of 4CT. Feasibility of that route: Low.

Critic gate: the Five Colour Theorem is proved in prose in F5_report.md. Euler's formula and the polygonal Jordan theorem are cited from Diestel, not derived. There is no Lean proof. The Four Colour Theorem is not proved.

Critic gate: bichromatic_reachable_iff_induce_delete is a Lean proof with no sorry. If c(v) is outside {a,b}, (a,b)-reachability in G is the same as in the induced subgraph on V\{v}. lake build was reported exit 0. This is not the Five Colour Theorem.

Critic gate: a simple plane triangulation is 3-colourable if and only if every degree is even. Proved in A3_report.md. The cache has exactly seven such triangulations through 11 vertices, each with P(G,3)=6. This is not the Four Colour Theorem.

Critic: the Birkhoff diamond and its Type C reducer were extracted from the notebooks as products of matchings. Cap (47,3) matches the printed colour checks. The census of 7210 coloured caps stays blocked: the witnesses live in Wolfram dumps and Mathematica is not installed. State-reducibility of the diamond is not proved in this repository.

S4b gives a second proof of the Eulerian-triangulation theorem already on t2-eulerian-tri: colour a noncrossing Eulerian circuit with 1,2,3. The cache again has exactly the same seven 3-colourable triangulations. Not a new theorem and not the Four Colour Theorem.

S3b repeats the RSST count independently: Birkhoff diamond, maximal consistent bad set empty (729 colourings, 96 extend); degree-5 vertex, 30 bad colourings remain, including (-1,-1,0,-1,1). The earlier contradictory flag in that file is gone. Free Kempe-component swaps accept both graphs and are not this test.

Critic gate: degree4_kempe_frees_colour compiles with no sorry. If the (a,b)-chain of one neighbour misses the neighbour coloured b, the swap is a proper 4-colouring and those four neighbours use at most three colours. Existence of that separated pair is not proved. The plane is still missing.

Critic gate: every Tait colouring of the dual of a triangulation on n>=4 vertices has sign (-1)^n. The proof is D3_report.md section 3; local_lemma checks the 24 Klein triples; the n<=11 orientation audit has no failures. The signed count is nonzero exactly when a colouring exists, so this does not prove the Four Colour Theorem.
The T_9,35 degree-4 witness was accepted on 27 September and left in progress. The exhibition is closed. The universal conjecture stays killed on t1-conj-d4.
Tilley's order-12 Kempe-locked triangulation stays blocked. arXiv:1809.02807 and the MDPI version give a figure and no edge list. The figure is not transcribed.

PlaneMap/Jordan and the conditional degree-five Kempe stack compile without sorry. Euler, the edge bound, degree at most five, neighbour rotation, even_is_face_sum, cycleEdgeCoeff_is_face_sum, local no-cross separation, and five_color_degree_five under hopposite are Lean theorems. The complete Lean Five Colour Theorem remains open on the connected Kempe-cycle bridge and vertex-deletion induction carrier. This is not the Four Colour Theorem.

The current-Mathlib PlaneMap stack now proves closed-walk face-sum parity, alternating-walk Heawood separation, degree-five neighbour rotation, and five_color_extension across any deleted vertex of degree at most five. DeleteVertex proves strict component-size decrease and colouring assembly; FiveColorExamples proves every PlaneMap 6 is five-colourable. The global five_color_theorem remains open on generated PlaneMap reconstruction for deleted components and a recursive low-degree premise that does not assume face-length preservation. This is not the Four Colour Theorem.

Compiled the general Five Colour Theorem for every generated PlaneMap with no face-length premise. node.title: Mass-macro descent
node.statement: For every finite simple spherical triangulation T of minimum degree at least 5, some degree-5 vertex r satisfies Good(T,r): every proper 4-colouring of T−r with p=1 has a sequence of at most two single-component swaps after which R is strictly smaller. Intermediate ranks may rise. Stop when p=0; q need not be 0.
node.approach: Existential claim only: for every T there exists r in D(T). Exterior roots of one anchor are a regression set, not the quantifier. Polynomial Select is a separate node. The rank is the existing component-mass formula, encoded as R=(6n²+1)p+q.
node.evidence: One-swap descent is killed at order-20 graph 36, root 8. Two-swap descent is computed only on that fixture. The corpus has not been run. 0≤R≤12n²+1, so a true claim needs at most that many macros. Across six colour pairs there are at most 3(n−1) bichromatic components; (6n)² is a conservative bound on testing one- and two-move sequences, not a proved solver cost. A failure does not refute four-colourability or bare reachability. The name D2 is the historical Penrose node and is not reused.
node.killCriteria: The existential claim dies only when every degree-5 root has a colouring with no decreasing macro. One bad root kills only Good(T,r). A set dies if it contains one bad root. A selector dies only if the root it returns is bad. Do not lengthen the macro past two to raise the pass rate.

node.title: Polynomial selection, separate from descent

node.evidence: Root 8 of graph 36 fails (σ, β) and passes the tested two-swap mass macro, so the other seven (σ, β) roots are not this selection target. (σ, β) depends on label-sensitive normalization.
node.killCriteria: The specified Select or tie-break returns a root that is not good. S(T)=D(T) fails as soon as any root fails; that is stronger than the existential claim and does not by itself refute it.

node.title: Breadcrumb descent
node.statement: Same class, degree-5 roots, component moves, and rank R as mass-macro descent, plus a run-local warning set. Wave 1 moves to the least-R unwarned state within two swaps. A dead end is warned and the run steps back one link. From the start, wave 2 moves to the least-R unwarned state in the whole radius-three ball and restarts. The frozen policy is breadcrumb-v1-global-min-depth3-canonical-lex. Ties use the canonical colour tuple on increasing vertex labels. Warning identities are colour orbits. The claim is that every triangulation has a degree-5 root at which every start reaches a target, and that warnings per run are polynomially bounded.
node.approach: A memory policy, sibling of mass-macro descent, not a replacement and not a longer mass macro. Depth three was chosen after the traps were observed, so a corpus pass is not a holdout. The canonical tie-break is label-dependent.
node.evidence: The finite corpus check is computed on the child node. It is not a theorem. The warning bound and relabelling invariance stay open. One root with no radius-three escape kills only that root's guarantee. The existential claim dies only when every degree-5 root has a failing start.

notes.text: From a prepared zero, the B gap 0, rho, tau, 0 repeats rho on u_i u_{i+1} and is discarded. The gap 0, tau, rho, 0 has link (1, rho, tau, rho, 0). On the icosahedron, every fan colouring of T-star reaches a link of at most three colours in one Kempe swap or one slide. Each fan has 8 orbits up to colour renaming: 2 already use three colours, and 6 use four. The same worst length holds at all 12 vertices. Slides alone can take two steps. The failing list is empty. This is a computation on one graph, not the vacancy hypothesis.

A fan-proper 5-cycle has two orbits. The word (0,1,0,1,2) already uses three colours. The word (0,1,0,2,3) is proper on three fans, and one Kempe swap reduces it only when a (1,2)-path or a (1,3)-path fails to join the link. On the 14-vertex gyroelongated hexagonal dipyramid with U0 deleted, both paths are present and either swap leaves four colours. The thirty-one edges of that deletion are proper. One Kempe swap is not forced.

On the icosahedron the six four-colour fan orbits each fall to three colours by one Kempe swap. Three of them also fall by one slide. The other three still have four colours after every slide from the deleted vertex, and slides alone take two steps. At that fixed vertex all 20 deletion orbits have Kempe distance at most 1. This count does not force the same swap on the dipyramid link.

node.title: Two mixed moves reduce to Kempe swaps
node.statement: On any finite simple graph, with any finite colour palette, if a deletion colouring reaches a missing link colour in at most two mixed moves, then the same number of Kempe swaps reaches one at the original hole.
node.approach: Accepted hand theorem. Terminal slides become singleton swaps. Two slides reduce to a slide and a swap, and that form either commutes to two swaps or collapses to one. No planarity or fan hypothesis is used. This is not a Lean compilation. The vacancy hypothesis is not this theorem.
node.evidence: Both parallel teams accepted the component argument. An independent check of 8,284 slide-then-swap target paths on four old fixtures passed. That check is consistency, not a census. The WP19 sources were not amended. A universal fill-length bound remains open.
node.killCriteria: A finite simple graph, a finite palette, and a deletion colouring whose mixed distance is 0, 1 or 2 while the Kempe distance at the original hole is different.

notes.text: Recorded as an accepted hand theorem. The green status is that acceptance. There is no Lean audit of this argument.
Colouring basics were proved so a Kempe swap had a proper colouring to act on. The degree-four step waits on chain equality, which is why those two are no longer siblings.
The core was proved so later nodes could start: Jordan separation, the rank bound, and deletion closure all use the generated map. They were not independent foundations.

The bridge was proved so the Five Colour Theorem could pass a degree-five vertex. Degree four did not need this bridge. The five-colour theorem is its child, and the four-colour problem at degree five is the route that remains.

The extension was proved so every spherical map on at most eleven vertices could be coloured by deleting a vertex of degree at most four. Gate B is that elimination, and it could not start as a theorem until the extension existed. The neighbour cycle is the step the extension reads.

Contact was proved so one empty dead-end root would finish the theorem. Mass descent, breadcrumb descent, and the rank search are attempts to empty that root. They hang off this theorem. A slide still does not plug into it, because the hole would move.
Gate E is the general spherical theorem, and it waits on D. The executable cost and the ordinary-planar bridge stay beside D, as the plan allowed.

Order 24 graph 7228 already has mixed distance 3 and Kempe distance 5, so the relation is not 'at most one extra swap'. This is not a new census.

node.killCriteria: A claimed identity between mixed length and Kempe length that fails on graph 7228, or a proof that no relation of any kind exists.

node.killCriteria: A rule that accepts a known bad root, or a proof that availability alone cannot yield a selector.

node.title: Infinite family with fan-selection length 3
node.statement: For every integer k at least 1, chaining k copies of order-17 graph 1 along two disjoint facial triangles yields a minimum-degree-5 spherical triangulation of order 14k+3 whose fan-selection length is exactly 3.
node.approach: Accepted hand theorem. The seed is the existing 17:1 certificate. Each join identifies a facial triangle, so a degree-5 root keeps its old link. The compiled short-fill theorem turns a global fill of length at most 2 into Kempe swaps that restrict to the seed and contradict it. No new order was generated. This is not compiled, and it does not bound m on every triangulation.
node.evidence: Orders 17, 31, 45, and so on. For k at least 2 the joins have degree at least 8. Both teams reviewed the clique-interface argument. The seed script rechecks the old witnesses. No graph with m at least 4 is known.
node.killCriteria: A gap in the restriction of a Kempe component across the triangular interface, or a chain whose fan-selection length is not 3.

notes.text: The kill of m at most 2 is not a single graph. Whether m stays bounded is open.

node.title: Three-move obstruction
node.statement: If a proper deletion colouring has no pure Kempe fill within three swaps, and a mixed path of length three reaches a filled link, then that path starts with a singleton slide, and every two-swap finish after the slide uses the slid colour.

patches.title: Termination and a polynomial algorithm for the vacancy induction (conditional plan)
patches.statement: Conditional on the vacancy hypothesis: the order drops by one per level and the fill step is a search on a finite space, so the algorithm stops; the vacancy hypothesis is needed only for success. Total running time is polynomial only if the fill length for the witness pair is bounded by a constant K, then O(N to the K+2) with a computable witness rule. A non-constant bound is not enough. Verifying a witness (every colouring has a path) has no known polynomial test. The data (kappa at most 5, orders 21 to 24) only suggests K near 5 [post hoc].

node.title: Conjecture L (lock persistence) and the F-orbit structure
node.statement: Conjecture L: there is an absolute N, data suggesting 5, such that no doubly locked state at a degree-5 hole has an F-chain of consecutive doubly locked iterates longer than N. A targetless component would give an infinite F-chain, so L would imply that every degree-5 vertex is clean, hence the vacancy hypothesis in the core. L is a local statement about G minus the hole. Open. One explicit planar chain of length 6 would refute it. Hand parts, unreviewed: F swaps the repeated colour with the three singleton colours so the repeat index runs 0, 3, 1, 4, 2; after five steps the pattern returns with the singleton colours permuted, so F-orbits on raw states have length divisible by 15.
node.approach: Math worker page MathVHLine.md, not reviewed line by line. Evidence is weak by the page's own account: chains of consecutive doubly locked iterates of length 4 (once 5), never 6, on a few thousand locked states of self-built random triangulations at orders 10 to 30. Short chains are also what happens when no targetless component exists. Suggested attack: the lock path of F(s) crossing the Jordan curve of the lock path at a gamma vertex outside the swapped component.
node.evidence: Under the gate on unreviewed pages this stays exploring. Conjecture L is open, not evidence for anything. Math takes it next unless redirected.

node.title: Lines K1 to K3 on the clean-vertex route, proposed killed

K1: "F to the fifth is the identity on locked states, decided by sampling or orbit counting": the literal version is false by item 1 of the page, and the renamed version (F to the fifth is a colour renaming of the whole colouring) has no testable instances. K2: counting or discharging on the known data (Theorems A, C, D, mobility, Euler) cannot give a clean vertex, since the abstract model "every off-face vertex unclean with a constant count" satisfies it. K3: pair confinement and any invariant of the repeat pair, since Theorem A moves every pair index to every other.

node.title: Conjecture L refuted as stated by finite certificates, pending replay by Math and the audit
node.statement: Conjecture L (an absolute bound N on chains of consecutive doubly locked F-iterates) is false as stated. Certificate W6: a 20-vertex plane triangulation (degrees 3 to 8) with a degree-5 hole v, where s, F(s), ..., F^5(s) are doubly locked and F^6(s) is not, so N = 5 fails. Certificate A_3: a 5-fold symmetric stacked-antiprism triangulation on 17 vertices (twelve of degree 5, five of degree 6) with a colouring whose F-orbit has period 60 on raw colours and all 60 states doubly locked, so no N works. The team also reports A_4 (22 vertices) and A_5 (27 vertices); those are team claims, not rechecked by the lead. This is NOT a counterexample to the vacancy hypothesis or to cleanness: on A_3 the Kempe class of such a state contains filled states (40 of 100 canonical states) and the Kempe distance to a filled state is 2 or 3 (team data, not rechecked by the lead). Math's own implication was one-directional, a targetless component gives an infinite chain, and the converse fails.
node.approach: Explicit finite objects, reproduced by the lead's own verifier lead_verify_L.py, which shares no code with the team's. The definitions are Math's (repeat index, doubly locked, F as the swap of the alpha-gamma component of x(j+2)). Status: computed, not killed. The ledger kills a universal claim on a finite counterexample only after an independent replay, and Math's check against its own definitions and the audit's replay are pending, so the parent node keeps its exploring status and this node is the recorded refutation candidate. W6 and A_3 were found by hill-climbing and by symmetry; the prototype search reached the kill before it was pre-registered, and Long Table says so. The repaired conjecture, a bounded Kempe radius to a filled state with infinity meaning targetless, is a conjecture and has no data beyond A_3 to A_5 and the sampled states.
node.evidence: Navigator check: the committed lead verifier, run now, prints chain length 6 for W6 with state 6 not doubly locked, and period 60 for A_3 on a 17-vertex graph with degrees as stated. node.title: Theorem H: icosahedral holes have Kempe radius at most 3 (hand proof pending review)
node.statement: Worker claim, hand proof NOT reviewed line by line by Math: at a degree-5 hole whose five neighbours also have degree 5 every doubly locked state has Kempe radius at most 3. It uses only the ball around the hole, so it would hold on A_r for every r. Mechanism: doubly locked states have one of three local ring-1 patterns R1, R2, R3; R2 dies after one F step, R3 is broken by recolouring three link vertices, and F sends R1 to R3 or to a non-locked state, so on an infinite F-orbit every second state is locally breakable. Bound 3 is sharp for the argument (A_3 has 10 radius-3 states). T4 has radius 4 because its hole has two adjacent degree-6 link vertices, which makes step 1 fail (partly hand, checked on two states). Open: radius 2 for all r at least 4; a bounded-ball treatment of holes with degree-6 neighbours; any bound beyond icosahedral holes (at least 4 from T4).
node.approach: Math ran an independent numerical check (its own script, random flips of A_3 and A_4 keeping minimum degree 5, then exhaustive radii): 28 graphs, 11 holes with five degree-5 neighbours, radii of 705 doubly locked states {2: 684, 3: 21}, none above 3, no targetless class. That tests the claim and does not prove it. Math's conditional reading: if H holds, such a hole is clean by Corollary B, but only in a protected-face-compatible form (the check so far covers faces disjoint from the closed neighbourhood of the hole), and only for triangulations containing a degree-5 vertex with five degree-5 neighbours; it says nothing for the general case. Killed lines in the page: "the a,b-swap of x1's component always breaks the lock", "the barrier is the recoloured lock path", "radius 2 from local data", and the verbatim extension of H to degree-6 neighbours (not claimed).

patches.title: Theorem H: icosahedral holes have Kempe radius at most 3 (accepted by hand, not compiled, not audited)
patches.statement: At a degree-5 hole whose five neighbours also have degree 5, every doubly locked state has Kempe radius at most 3. It uses only the ball around the hole, not r, the A_r symmetry or Lemma B. Steps, as reviewed: R2, F(s) is not doubly locked; R3, the {a,b}-component is exactly {x0, x1, x2}, so the breaker is one legal whole-component swap, not a composition; R1, F(s) is not doubly locked or has pattern R3; so on an infinite F-orbit the pattern alternates and every second state is locally breakable. Two wording fixes made as an erratum to MathRadiusGeometry.md: step 4 uses the existence of P2 as a Jordan curve separating x0 from x2 and x3, so "no lock path beyond first or last vertex" was imprecise; and the distinctness of the w_t (no separating triangle) must be stated as a hypothesis. T4 is not covered: its hole has two adjacent degree-6 link vertices and radius 4.

node.title: Pathway sprint: routes to VH-exists
node.statement: From 11:50 on 6 October the main effort is pathways to the vacancy hypothesis: ideas, small hand examples and quick trial and error. Search is a kill test for an idea, not the work itself. Starting points named by the coordinator: mobility (compiled), fills next to a degree at most 4 vertex (hand), Theorem H (hand), degree at least 6 on separating triangles and the 4-connected least failure of the face-avoiding form (hand), the kill of lock persistence with fills still at radius 2 or 3 on every all-locked orbit found, and the existential freedom in the vertex, the fan and partly the colouring through T*.
node.approach: Coordinator's sprint on the user's direction (11:49, quoted: "it seems like we are working on brute force search instead of intuition and trial and error on novel strategies to show pathways"). Rules: an idea is a one-page sketch (claim, why it might hold, a hand example, a kill test); kill tests run at most 10 CPU-minutes on spent orders or explicit small graphs, labelled post hoc or exploratory, need no declaration and are never evidence for a theorem; a quick kill is a success; report every two hours or when an idea dies or survives its first test; the navigator adds each pathway as an exploring node and records kills fast. Compute: running jobs finish (P1 --all check, the Studio P1 replay T2, the WP21 cross-checks, the audit P1 replay); S2 (WP22) and Math's radius census are DEFERRED unless a pathway needs one as a kill test; no new census starts without a pathway that asks for it.

notes.text: Revision 113, Math 11:52 and 11:53 and the audit 11:53 (P-E). The first discharging plan fails: the icosahedral class (5,5,5,5,5) is NOT unavoidable. The pentakis dodecahedron (order 32, degrees 5 and 6, no 5-5 edge) and the Goldberg-type family have only (6,6,6,6,6) holes, so every unavoidable list must contain (6,6,6,6,6) or a class it lies in. Found independently by Math and the audit [hand, plus checked by the audit's pentakis.py]; the claim "(5^5) is unavoidable" is killed, recorded as a note, not a separate node. The audit adds that Theorem H's class is absent from every minimum-degree-5 triangulation of orders 14 to 16 and from most graphs at orders 17 to 22 [exploratory, plantri], and that "next to a degree at most 4 vertex" is vacuous in the core. [exploratory, post hoc] radius by link class over all minimum-degree-5 triangulations of orders 12 to 20 plus the pentakis dodecahedron: 28 classes, no targetless class, maximum radius 4 in exactly six classes ((5,5,5,5,6), (5,5,5,6,6), (5,5,5,6,7), (5,5,6,5,6), (5,5,6,5,7), (5,6,5,6,6)); (5,5,5,5,5) maximum 3, consistent with Theorem H; (6,6,6,6,6) maximum 2. Pentakis hole, by Math and independently by the audit: 4840 states of T minus x up to renaming, 3190 filled, 1520 at radius 1, 130 at radius 2 (130 doubly locked, all radius 2), none targetless. P-A thus reduces to Conjecture R class by class.
